messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High P95 latency spike detected for model-service/chi-2-prod in us-west-2. P95 -> 1.8s (baseline 300ms). Auto-escalation to #eng-runtime.
alex: saw this, noise across multiple hosts. metrics look correlated with kernel-selector v2 rollout.
priya: confirming — kernel-selector started gradual rollout ~2h ago. I'm seeing a sharp increase in kernel_fallback_count and memcpy_stall in the GPU telemetry.
martin: did the rollout change the primary kernel or just the heuristics?
priya: heuristics + new kernel choice for LLM-attn fused path. New path reduces perf for long-context patterns we didn't flag.
jen: kv-cache hit-rate dropped on the affected pools too, weird. Could be eviction churn from batching changes.
santiago: attaching quick profile dump I grabbed from one host:```topk: gpu_memcpy_stall 42%
       kernel_exec 28%
       wait_io 15%
kv_cache: miss_rate 18% (norm ~3%)
batching: avg_batch_size down 12% but enqueue_latency up 90ms```
priya: thanks. That memcpy_stall + kv miss implies the new kernel is thrashing memory layout and increasing micro-pauses — causes cache TTLs to expire and evictions.
alex: impact matrix: latency spike -> errors on streaming endpoints for small seq lengths, throughput drop for high-concurrency tenants. Customer-facing errors reported by support.
ops: adding mitigation options: 1) rollback kernel-selector to v1; 2) flip feature-flag to disable new batching heuristics; 3) route heavy tenants to dedicated pool; 4) temporary throttling for low-priority traffic.
martin: prefer non-rollback first: flip batching flag and enable kv-cache-pin for hot prefixes if possible. Cheap and reversible.
priya: batching flag toggle is ready: `flags.edge.batch_heuristics_v2=false`. KV pinning needs a small config push but can be done in 10m.
jen: routing heavy tenants off the shared pool now. I'll add a routing rule: `route:tenant.blacklist=[acct-188, acct-205]` to the shared autoscaler.
santiago: rolling the batching flag off on 6 hosts now, watching p95.
incident-bot: status update: mitigation in progress — batching_heuristics toggled on subset.
(2m later) priya: p95 dropped to 420ms on toggled hosts. memcpy_stall down to 8%. KV miss-rate trending back to baseline.
alex: great. keep throttles / routing in place until we have full rollback or new kernel patch.
martin: I'm going to open a perf follow-up ticket: root cause looks like kernel memory layout assumptions + batching timing interacting with KV cache eviction policy. We need deterministic unit tests with long-context synthetic workloads.
jen: also capture tenant priority mix in the incident timeline. This looked amplified by two heavy tenants concurrently hitting prefix-heavy workloads.
ops: leaving throttles for 30 more minutes, then re-evaluate.
priya: postmortem action items I'll own: (1) revert kernel-selector rollout until fix; (2) add integration perf-test that simulates KV TTL churn; (3) add alert for memcpy_stall >20% in kernel telemetry; (4) document safe rollback playbook.
alex: thanks all. I'll prepare customer comms draft for support.
incident-bot: incident resolved -> performance normalized after batching flag toggle + tenant routing. Monitoring for 1h.
(ongoing) santiago: note for follow-up: we should include a canary workload that mirrors real multi-tenant hot-prefix patterns when we validate kernel changes.
